# Module `ldp.capture`

> Output frame capture: the client-facing surface behind screenshots and remote mirroring. Binding the global capture manager and sending `grab` yields one `frame` event whose descriptor is a read-once snapshot of the output's current content — premultiplied ARGB8888 words, `width` x `height`, row-major, exactly the scanout a display would present. The capture never tears (the snapshot is taken between frames) and never blocks the frame pipeline (the content is copied out under the render lock, not mapped from live scanout).

Version range **1–1** · 1 interfaces · 1 requests · 2 events · 1 enums · 0 bitsets.

Why a grab could not produce a frame.

| Name | Value |
|---|---:|
| `out_of_memory` | 1 |
| `no_output` | 2 |

## Interfaces

### `ldp.capture.capture_manager`

The global entry point for output capture. One `grab` request produces at most one event: `frame` on success, `failed` on a resource error. The snapshot descriptor is read-once shared memory: read it to EOF (the size is `width * height * 4` bytes) and keep or drop it — the compositor never mutates a shipped frame.

*global (registry-advertised)*
